metadata.title: Student teachers’ responsible use of ICT: Examining two samples in Spain and Norway

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study used a non-random, convenience-style sampling approach by inviting all first-year student teachers entering three teacher education institutions in Spain and Norway to complete an online Webquest survey. The analytic sample consists of respondents with complete answers to all eight survey items; the authors report no missing responses for any item. The manuscript does not report the use of complex survey weights (e.g., sampling/design weights) or replicate-weight procedures, and it does not name any weight variables. Because the analysis is based on SEM/measurement invariance rather than ML prediction, the paper provides no guidance on applying PV-based weighting conventions from ILSA microdata; therefore, weighting is treated as not reported.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are not applicable because the dependent variables are self-reported Likert-scale survey constructs (perceived competence in privacy issues, cyberbullying handling, and ability to evaluate digital content), not cognitive achievement scores generated with PVs. Missing-data handling is effectively not needed for the eight items because the authors state there were no missing responses for any item, but they do not explicitly describe a formal missing-data procedure beyond that statement. Therefore, the missing-data handling field is set to not_reported due to limited methodological transparency about any broader exclusion rules (e.g., survey dropouts) beyond item-level missingness.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Participants were first-year student teachers from three universities (one Spanish university and two Norwegian universities). The authors used non-random sampling by inviting all student teachers entering the first year at the participating institutions. The survey was administered in Spain face-to-face in 18 groups over three weeks; in Norway it was administered either in small groups during obligatory classes or via a link provided in an introductory lecture, with 15–30 minutes to complete. The analytic dataset includes respondents with complete responses to all eight survey items; the authors report no missing responses for any of the eight items.

main_findings.dataset_used: ICILS 2013 (questionnaire adaptation) + DICTE Webquest survey (Spain & Norway student teachers, first-year)
main_findings.target_variable: Perceived competence in privacy issues (SEM factor)
main_findings.performance_metrics: SEM model fit (Spanish sample N=681): Chi-square=22.15 (p>0.13), CFI=0.996, TLI=0.994, RMSEA=0.024, SRMR=0.024. SEM model fit (Norwegian sample N=563): Chi-square=13.63 (p>0.62), CFI=1.000, TLI=1.000, RMSEA=0.000, SRMR=0.015. Factor loadings for privacy items: all >0.60 in both samples.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ICILS 2013 questionnaire adaptation within the DICTE Webquest survey data from first-year student teachers in Spain (N=681) and Norway (N=563), the study leveraged perceived competence in cyberbullying and ability to evaluate digital content to model perceived competence in privacy issues, finding a strong positive relationship between privacy competence and cyberbullying-handling competence (r=0.69 in Spain; r=0.57 in Norway) and a moderate relationship between privacy competence and digital content evaluation (r=0.34 in Spain; r=0.43 in Norway). This indicates that initial teacher education should treat privacy competence and related responsible-ICT competencies as an integrated set rather than isolated topics.

main_findings.dataset_used: ICILS 2013 (questionnaire adaptation) + DICTE Webquest survey (Spain & Norway student teachers, first-year)
main_findings.target_variable: Perceived competence in handling cyberbullying (SEM factor)
main_findings.performance_metrics: SEM model fit (Spanish sample N=681): Chi-square=22.15 (p>0.13), CFI=0.996, TLI=0.994, RMSEA=0.024, SRMR=0.024. SEM model fit (Norwegian sample N=563): Chi-square=13.63 (p>0.62), CFI=1.000, TLI=1.000, RMSEA=0.000, SRMR=0.015. Factor loadings for cyberbullying items: Spanish >0.80; Norwegian between 0.59 and 0.78.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ICILS 2013 questionnaire adaptation within the DICTE Webquest survey data from first-year student teachers in Spain (N=681) and Norway (N=563), the study leveraged perceived competence in privacy and ability to evaluate digital content to model perceived competence in handling cyberbullying, finding a strong positive relationship between privacy competence and cyberbullying-handling competence (r=0.69 in Spain; r=0.57 in Norway) and a weak relationship between cyberbullying-handling competence and digital content evaluation (r=0.19 in Spain; r=0.21 in Norway). This indicates that teacher education should prioritize privacy-linked ethical awareness when designing cyberbullying training, while also providing separate instruction for source evaluation skills.

main_findings.dataset_used: ICILS 2013 (questionnaire adaptation) + DICTE Webquest survey (Spain & Norway student teachers, first-year)
main_findings.target_variable: Ability to evaluate digital content (SEM factor)
main_findings.performance_metrics: SEM model fit (Spanish sample N=681): Chi-square=22.15 (p>0.13), CFI=0.996, TLI=0.994, RMSEA=0.024, SRMR=0.024. SEM model fit (Norwegian sample N=563): Chi-square=13.63 (p>0.62), CFI=1.000, TLI=1.000, RMSEA=0.000, SRMR=0.015. Correlations: privacy vs evaluation r=0.34 (Spain) and r=0.43 (Norway); cyberbullying vs evaluation r=0.19 (Spain) and r=0.21 (Norway).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ICILS 2013 questionnaire adaptation within the DICTE Webquest survey data from first-year student teachers in Spain (N=681) and Norway (N=563), the study leveraged perceived competence in privacy and perceived competence in cyberbullying to model ability to evaluate digital content, finding a moderate positive relationship with privacy competence (r=0.34 in Spain; r=0.43 in Norway) and a weak positive relationship with cyberbullying-handling competence (r=0.19 in Spain; r=0.21 in Norway). This indicates that responsible-ICT curricula should explicitly teach source evaluation as a distinct competency, even though it shares some ethical foundations with privacy.

data.outcome_summary: This study used a DICTE project Webquest survey administered to first-year student teachers in Spain (N=681) and Norway (N=563), adapting items from the ICILS 2013 questionnaire for privacy and cyberbullying constructs and from the Norwegian Monitor 2011 for digital content evaluation. The authors analyzed the three latent constructs using structural equation modeling and tested measurement invariance across the two country samples. Model fit was acceptable in both samples (e.g., Spanish: CFI=0.996, RMSEA=0.024, SRMR=0.024; Norwegian: CFI=1.000, RMSEA=0.000, SRMR=0.015). Correlations showed strong privacy–cyberbullying links (r=0.69 Spain; r=0.57 Norway), moderate privacy–evaluation links (r=0.34 Spain; r=0.43 Norway), and weak cyberbullying–evaluation links (r=0.19 Spain; r=0.21 Norway). The paper is not an ML prediction study (no ML algorithms, no PVs), and it reports no missing item responses, limiting concerns about missing-data bias but not about self-report validity or cross-country comparability.
